title: Segamat Earthquake Quiz
description: Watched "What caused the Segamat earthquakes?" See if you can tell interplate and intraplate quakes apart.

questions.question: Most big earthquakes in Japan and Indonesia are which type?
questions.explanation: Japan and Indonesia sit on plate boundaries, and most of their big quakes happen where two plates push against each other, so they are interplate earthquakes.

questions.question: Segamat is far from any plate boundary. What type was this earthquake?
questions.explanation: Earthquakes inside a plate, far from its edges, are called intraplate earthquakes. They are rarer, and their causes are harder to pin down.

questions.question: When seismic waves from a distant earthquake pass by and briefly change the forces on a fault, what is that called?
questions.explanation: Dynamic stress is the brief push and pull from passing seismic waves. Static stress is the permanent change left behind after a nearby fault slips.

questions.question: Why might underground fluids (like water) trigger an earthquake?
options: They raise pore pressure, "lubricating" the fault so it slips more easily
questions.explanation: Fluid seeping into a fault raises the pore pressure, which offsets the force clamping the fault together, so it slips more easily.

questions.question: Which Japanese earthquake does the video use as an example of fluids being linked to earthquakes?
questions.explanation: The Noto Peninsula had years of earthquake swarms before the big quake, and research links them to fluids rising from deep underground.
